blocks.text: Pichle sabaq ka natija yaad kijiye: function ka barhna ya ghatna sirf do qisam ki jagahon par badal sakta hai: jahan \(f'(x) = 0\) ho, ya jahan \(f'(x)\) exist hi na kare. Ab hum in dono ko ek naam dete hain: critical point. Phir inhi ki madad se ek pakka tareeqa seekhenge jis se kisi bhi function ke increasing aur decreasing intervals nikal aate hain. Yeh tareeqa exam mein bohat aata hai: Exercise 2.4 ka pehla sawal isi par hai, aur aage maximum aur minimum dhoondne ka kaam bhi isi par khara hai. Is liye har step dhyan se samajhiye, ratta mat lagaiye.

Kitab ki definition: function \(f(x)\) ke liye point \(x = c\), jahan \(c \in \operatorname{Dom} f\), critical point kehlata hai agar:
\[f'(c) = 0 \text{ or } f'(c) \text{ does not exist.}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Critical points hi woh jagahein hain jahan \(f\) barhne se ghatne (ya ghatne se barhne) mein badal sakta hai. Shart \(c \in \operatorname{Dom} f\) bohat ahem hai: \(f(x) = \frac{1}{x}\) mein \(f'(0)\) exist nahin karta, lekin 0 to domain mein hi nahin (\(\frac{1}{0}\) undefined hai), is liye 0 critical point nahin. Pehle dekhiye point domain mein hai ya nahin.
Examples:

items: \(f(x) = |x|\) ke liye \(x = 0\) par derivative exist nahin karta, is liye \(x = 0\) critical point hai.
\(f(x) = x^{2}\) ke liye derivative \(f'(x) = 2x\) point \(x = 0\) par zero hai, is liye \(x = 0\) critical point hai.

blocks.text: Method to Find Intervals Where a Function is Increasing or Decreasing
Kisi function ke increasing ya decreasing intervals nikaalne ke liye yeh steps follow karein:

items: Step 1: Diye gaye function \(f(x)\) ka derivative \(f'(x)\) nikaalein.
Step 2: \(f'(x) = 0\) hal kar ke, aur woh points pehchaan kar jahan \(f'(x)\) exist nahin karta, critical points nikaalein.
Step 3: Agar critical points hain, to un ki madad se domain ko chhote intervals (sub-intervals) mein baant dein.
Step 4: Har sub-interval se ek test point chun kar \(f'(x)\) mein rakhein:
Agar kisi sub-interval mein \(f'(x) > 0\), to function wahan increasing hai.
Agar kisi sub-interval mein \(f'(x) < 0\), to function wahan decreasing hai.

blocks.title: Point to Note
blocks.text: Critical points se bane domain ke har sub-interval mein derivative ka sign ek jaisa rehta hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Har step ka maqsad samajh lijiye, phir yeh tareeqa kabhi nahin bhoolega:
Step 1: \(f'(x)\) slope ka formula hai; isi ke sign se charhai ya utraai ka pata chalta hai.
Step 2: critical points sarhad ki chowkiyan hain; sirf inhi par sign badal sakta hai. Dono qisam dhoondni hain: \(f' = 0\) wale aur \(f'\) undefined wale.
Step 3: number line ko in chowkiyon par kaat dein, jaise ek rassi ko nishaanon par kaat kar tukre bana lete hain.
Step 4: har tukre mein se koi bhi ek aasaan number utha kar \(f'\) mein rakhein; jo sign aaye wohi poore tukre ka hukm hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Ek hi test point kyun kaafi hai? Continuous \(f'\) ka sign badalne ke liye use ya to 0 se guzarna parega ya kisi aisi jagah se jahan \(f'\) exist na kare, yani kisi critical point se. Sub-interval ke andar koi critical point nahin, is liye ek point par jo sign mila wohi poore tukre ka sign hai. Socho jaise ek kamre ka darwaza: kamre ke andar kahin bhi khare hon, aap usi kamre mein hain. Test point hamesha aasaan chuniye (0, \(\pm 1\), poore numbers).

blocks.title: Numbering note
blocks.text: "Example 12" ka label yahan doosri dafa chhapa hai (pehla Example 12 section 2.8 mein hai). Is ke baad kitab seedha Example 19 par chali jati hai: Examples 17 aur 18 chhape hi nahin. Hum printed numbers hi rakhte hain.

blocks.title: Example 12
blocks.problem: Find the intervals in which the function \(f(x) = 2x^{3} - 3x^{2} - 12x\) is increasing or decreasing.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = 2x^{3} - 3x^{2} - 12x\).
Maloom karna: kin intervals mein \(f\) barhta hai aur kin mein ghatta hai.
Tareeqa: upar wale chaar steps: derivative, critical points, intervals mein taqseem, har interval mein ek test point.

Step 1: Domain aur derivative
Function har \(x \in \mathbb{R} = (-\infty, \infty)\) ke liye defined hai (polynomial hai). \(x\) ke lehaaz se derivative:
\[f'(x) = 6x^{2} - 6x - 12 \quad \text{...(1)}\]
Kyun: har term par power rule: \(\frac{d}{dx}(2x^{3}) = 6x^{2}\), \(\frac{d}{dx}(3x^{2}) = 6x\), \(\frac{d}{dx}(12x) = 12\).

Step 2: Kahan \(f'\) exist nahin karta?
Equation (1) se saaf hai ke \(f'(x)\) har real \(x\) ke liye defined hai.
Kyun: \(f'\) khud ek polynomial hai, aur polynomial har real number par value deta hai. Is liye yahan critical points sirf \(f'(x) = 0\) se aayenge.

Step 3: \(f'(x) = 0\) hal karein
\[6x^{2} - 6x - 12 = 0\]
\[6(x^{2} - x - 2) = 0\]
\[6(x + 1)(x - 2) = 0\]
\[x = -1 \quad \text{and} \quad x = 2\]
Kyun: pehle common factor 6 bahar nikala, phir factorise kiya: woh do numbers jin ka product \(-2\) aur sum \(-1\) ho, \(-2\) aur \(1\) hain.

Step 4: Intervals banayein
To \(x = -1\) aur \(x = 2\) critical points hain. Inhein real line par mark karein (Figure 2.1); yeh domain ko teen tukron mein baant dete hain: \((-\infty, -1)\), \((-1, 2)\) aur \((2, \infty)\).
Kyun: \(f'\) ka sign sirf critical point par badal sakta hai, is liye har tukre ke andar sign ek hi rehta hai.

Step 5: Har tukre mein ek test point
\[f'(-2) = 6(4) + 12 - 12 = 24 > 0\]
\[f'(0) = 0 - 0 - 12 = -12 < 0\]
\[f'(3) = 54 - 18 - 12 = 24 > 0\]
Kyun: har tukre ka sign ek hi point se pata chal jata hai (Point to Note).
Dhyan dein: \(-6(-2) = +12\) hai; negative test point par sign ki ghalti sab se zyada hoti hai. Kitab ki table beech wali value \(12 < 0\) chhaapti hai; sahi \(-12\) hai.

Step 6: Natija
\((-\infty, -1)\) aur \((2, \infty)\) par \(f'(x) > 0\): yahan increasing. \((-1, 2)\) par \(f'(x) < 0\): yahan decreasing.
Kyun: 2.9 ka test.

Tasdeeq: \(f(-2) = -16 - 12 + 24 = -4\), \(f(-1) = -2 - 3 + 12 = 7\), \(f(2) = 16 - 12 - 24 = -20\), \(f(3) = 54 - 27 - 36 = -9\).
Values \(-4\) se 7 tak barhin, 7 se \(-20\) tak ghatin, phir \(-9\) tak barhin: bilkul increasing, decreasing, increasing.
blocks.answer: \(f(x) = 2x^{3} - 3x^{2} - 12x\) intervals \((-\infty, -1)\) aur \((2, \infty)\) par increasing, aur \((-1, 2)\) par decreasing hai.

blocks.alt: A number line from minus infinity to plus infinity with two marked points, x = minus 1 and x = 2, which split it into the intervals minus infinity to minus 1, minus 1 to 2, and 2 to infinity.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.1: the critical points x = −1 and x = 2 on the real line (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Ab har sub-interval mein \(f'(x)\) ka sign check karte hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki table mein \(f'(0) = 6(0)^{2} - 6(0) - 12 = 12 < 0\) chhapa hai. Value \(12\) nahin balke \(-12\) hai: \(6(0)^{2} - 6(0) - 12 = -12 < 0\). Natija (\((-1, 2)\) par decreasing) sahi hai.

Is liye function \(f(x) = 2x^{3} - 3x^{2} - 12x\):
\((-\infty, -1)\) aur \((2, \infty)\) par increasing hai; \((-1, 2)\) par decreasing hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Example 12 se agle sabaq (2.10) ki ek jhalak bhi mil jati hai. \(x = -1\) par function barhne se ghatne lagta hai: yeh ek chotti (peak) hai, aur wahan \(f(-1) = 7\). \(x = 2\) par function ghatne se barhne lagta hai: yeh ek wadi (valley) hai, aur wahan \(f(2) = -20\).
Yani critical points sirf intervals ki sarhad nahin, balke graph ki chottiyan aur wadiyan bhi yahin milti hain. Agle sabaq mein inhi ko local maximum aur local minimum kahenge, aur inhein dhoondne ke mazeed tareeqe seekhenge.
Ek baat aur: test point ki value (jaise 24 ya \(-12\)) ki miqdaar se koi farq nahin parta; sirf us ka sign (plus ya minus) kaam ka hai.

blocks.title: Example 19
blocks.problem: Find the intervals where the function \(f(x) = x^{\frac{2}{3}}\) is increasing or decreasing on the domain \(x \in (-\infty, \infty)\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = x^{\frac{2}{3}}\), poori real line par.
Maloom karna: \(f\) kahan barhta hai aur kahan ghatta hai.
Tareeqa: wohi chaar steps. Farq yeh hai ke is dafa critical point \(f'(x) = 0\) se nahin, balke us jagah se aayega jahan \(f'\) exist hi nahin karta.

Step 1: Derivative
\[f'(x) = \dfrac{2}{3}x^{-\frac{1}{3}}\]
\[= \dfrac{2}{3x^{\frac{1}{3}}} \quad \text{...(1)}\]
Kyun: power rule \(\frac{d}{dx}x^{n} = nx^{n-1}\), jahan \(n = \frac{2}{3}\) aur \(\frac{2}{3} - 1 = -\frac{1}{3}\). Negative power denominator mein chali jati hai.

Step 2: Kahan \(f'\) exist nahin karta?
Equation (1) mein \(x = 0\) rakhein to denominator zero ho jata hai, is liye \(f'(0)\) defined nahin. Lekin \(f(0) = 0\) maujood hai, yani 0 domain mein hai. Is liye \(x = 0\) critical point hai.
Kyun: critical point ki shart hai \(c \in \operatorname{Dom} f\) aur \(f'(c)\) exist na kare; dono baatein poori hain.

Step 3: \(f'(x) = 0\) hal karein
\[\dfrac{2}{3x^{\frac{1}{3}}} = 0\]
Is equation ka koi hal nahin. To sirf ek critical point \(x = 0\) hai, jo domain ko \((-\infty, 0)\) aur \((0, \infty)\) mein baant deta hai.
Kyun: koi fraction tabhi zero hoti hai jab numerator zero ho; yahan numerator 2 hai, jo kabhi zero nahin.

Step 4: \((-\infty, 0)\) mein test point \(x = -1\)
\[f'(-1) = \dfrac{2}{3(-1)^{\frac{1}{3}}} = -\dfrac{2}{3} < 0\]
Yani poore \((-\infty, 0)\) par \(f'(x) < 0\): \(f\) yahan decreasing hai.
Kyun: \((-1)^{\frac{1}{3}} = -1\), kyun ke \((-1)^{3} = -1\). Negative number ka cube root negative hota hai.
Dhyan dein: kai calculators \((-1)^{1/3}\) par error dete hain; hath se sochiye.

Step 5: \((0, \infty)\) mein test point \(x = 1\)
\[f'(1) = \dfrac{2}{3(1)^{\frac{1}{3}}} = \dfrac{2}{3} > 0\]
Yani poore \((0, \infty)\) par \(f'(x) > 0\): \(f\) yahan increasing hai.
Kyun: test point usi interval se lena hota hai jise test kar rahe hain; \(1 \in (0, \infty)\). (Kitab yahan ghalti se \((-\infty, 0)\) likhti hai, neeche dekhiye.)

Tasdeeq: \(f(-8) = \left((-8)^{\frac{1}{3}}\right)^{2} = (-2)^{2} = 4\), \(f(-1) = 1\), \(f(0) = 0\), \(f(1) = 1\), \(f(8) = 4\).
Values 0 tak girti hain aur phir uthti hain: pehle decreasing, phir increasing. Origin par graph ki nok (cusp) hai, isi liye wahan \(f'(0)\) exist nahin karta.
blocks.answer: \(f(x) = x^{\frac{2}{3}}\) interval \((-\infty, 0)\) par decreasing aur \((0, \infty)\) par increasing hai; is ka akela critical point \(x = 0\) hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 19 mein kitab "Choose \(x = 1 \in (-\infty, 0)\)" likhti hai. Test point 1 to interval \((0, \infty)\) ka hissa hai; sahi "Choose \(x = 1 \in (0, \infty)\)" hai. Baaqi hisaab aur natija (\((0, \infty)\) par increasing) sahi hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
\(f(x) = x^{2} - 6x + 5\) lijiye. \(f'(x) = 2x - 6\), jo har jagah exist karta hai.
\(2x - 6 = 0\) se \(x = 3\): ek hi critical point. Tukre: \((-\infty, 3)\) aur \((3, \infty)\).
Test: \(f'(0) = -6 < 0\) (decreasing), \(f'(4) = 2 > 0\) (increasing).
Yani parabola 3 tak neeche aata hai aur phir upar jata hai; \(x = 3\) us ka sab se neeche wala point hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Example 19 aur Example 16 (\(|x|\)) mein ek dilchasp farq hai. \(|x|\) ka graph origin par ek V jaisa kona banata hai, jab ke \(x^{2/3}\) ka graph wahan ek nokeeli chonch (cusp) banata hai: dono taraf se graph khara (vertical) ho kar origin tak aata hai, is liye wahan slope ki koi finite value nahin. Dono haalaton mein natija ek hai: derivative exist nahin karta, phir bhi point domain mein hai, is liye woh critical point hai aur function wahan ghatne se barhne lagta hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(f(x) = x^{3} - 3x\) ke increasing aur decreasing intervals kya hain? (Jawab: \(f'(x) = 3x^{2} - 3 = 3(x - 1)(x + 1)\), critical points \(x = -1, 1\). Test: \(f'(-2) = 9 > 0\), \(f'(0) = -3 < 0\), \(f'(2) = 9 > 0\). Yani \((-\infty, -1)\) aur \((1, \infty)\) par increasing, \((-1, 1)\) par decreasing.)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(f(x) = x^{3}\) ka critical point kahan hai, aur kya wahan function ka rawaiya badalta hai? (Jawab: \(f'(x) = 3x^{2} = 0\) se \(x = 0\). Lekin \(f'(-1) = 3 > 0\) aur \(f'(1) = 3 > 0\): dono taraf increasing. Critical point hona zaroori shart hai, magar wahan rawaiya badalna zaroori nahin. Is liye har critical point ke dono taraf test karna parta hai; sirf critical point mil jane se faisla nahin hota.)

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Sign test ko kitab ki tarah table mein likhiye (Interval | Test point | Sign of \(f'(x)\) | Conclusion). Examiner har critical point, har sub-interval aur har ek ka saaf natija dekhta hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Critical point: \(c \in \operatorname{Dom} f\) jahan \(f'(c) = 0\) ho ya \(f'(c)\) exist na kare.
2. Tareeqa: \(f'\) nikaalo, critical points nikaalo, domain baanto, har tukre mein ek test point.
3. Har tukre ke andar \(f'\) ka sign ek jaisa rehta hai.
4. \(2x^{3} - 3x^{2} - 12x\): \((-\infty, -1)\), \((2, \infty)\) par increasing; \((-1, 2)\) par decreasing.
5. \(x^{2/3}\): \((-\infty, 0)\) par decreasing, \((0, \infty)\) par increasing; is ka critical point \(f'(0)\) ke exist na karne se aata hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Sirf \(f'(x) = 0\) hal karna aur woh points bhool jana jahan \(f'\) exist nahin karta (Example 19 mein phir koi critical point hi na milta).
2. Test point ko us ke interval se bahar, ya bilkul critical point par le lena.
3. Negative test points par sign ki ghalti: \(-6(-2) = +12\), aur \((-1)^{1/3} = -1\).
